caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: San Marino's debt went from 14.2% of GDP in 2006 (12.6% in 2007, the low) to 77.2% in 2021, the series peak, on the banking-sector clean-up and COVID — the state absorbed failed banks' losses. It fell to 70.6% in 2022 and is projected at 60.6% in 2025 (69.8% in 2020). GDP is tiny and flat: $1.9bn in 2006, a projected $2.2bn in 2025. The IMF program of 2020-22 anchored the adjustment. Debt is falling and the banking clean-up is largely done; sustainability is adequate for a microstate with no monetary autonomy.
inflation_management: San Marino uses the euro under a monetary agreement with Italy, importing ECB conditions. Inflation was 2.4% in 2009, -0.1% in 2020 (the low), 5.3% in 2022, then 5.9% in 2023, the series high — the peak came a year later than the euro area's, reflecting local pass-through lags. It fell to 1.2% in 2024 and is projected at 2.3% for 2025, near target. With no central bank, there is no domestic monetary lever; the inflation story is entirely imported.

key_events.event: Banking crisis: the state absorbed failed banks, beginning the debt climb from 14.2% of GDP.
Tax-transparency reforms ended the banking-secrecy model; the financial center shrank.
IMF program (2020-22) anchored the post-COVID and banking-crisis adjustment.
Inflation peaked at 5.9%, a year later than the euro-area peak, on pass-through lags.
Debt projected at 60.6% of GDP, down from the 77.2% peak, as the banking clean-up concluded.

outlook_next_decade: San Marino's outlook is stable but narrow: the banking clean-up is done, debt is falling, and the euro agreement provides monetary credibility. The economy's smallness is the permanent constraint — tourism, manufacturing niches, and financial services must carry it. EU association talks are the main structural lever. Inflation will track the euro area. The analytical assessment: repaired and stable, with limited growth levers beyond integration.
